candidates.evidence: Strongest sample line (368.7 cm-1) and a second strong line (263.5 cm-1) fit the MPS3 pattern of a strongest mode near 370-385 and a medium mode near 275-280 (Lee et al. arXiv:1608.04169 Fig. S7 at 300 K: P6 ~372-378, P5 ~275-280; Kim et al. arXiv:1906.05802 Fig. S3 at 290 K: ~383 strongest, ~280 medium). But the strong modes sit 3-14 cm-1 (368.7 vs 372-383) and 12-17 cm-1 (263.5 vs 275-280) below the FePS3 positions, the 123.5 cm-1 broad band has no counterpart (FePS3 broad hump ~100 cm-1), and the 263.5 line is much stronger relative to the 368.7 line than the FePS3 medium mode is. Silicon is calibrated (520.9 vs 520.7), so a calibration offset cannot explain the gap.

Kim et al. arXiv:1906.05802 Fig. S3 (290 K): MnPS3 strongest line ~275 cm-1 with a ~385 cm-1 line and weak ~155 and ~246 cm-1 lines. The sample's 263.5 cm-1 line is ~11 cm-1 below the MnPS3 ~275 line, and the 368.7 cm-1 line is ~16 cm-1 below ~385. MnPS3 has no strong line at ~124 cm-1 or ~551 cm-1 in the 290 K data, and the ~155 cm-1 line is absent in the sample.

Kim et al. arXiv:1906.05802 Fig. S3 (290 K): NiPS3 lines at ~131, ~177, ~256, ~280 and ~386 cm-1. The sample has no lines at ~131 or ~177 cm-1, and its strongest line (368.7 cm-1) is ~17 cm-1 below the NiPS3 ~386 cm-1 line.

hint_reasoning: The spectrum shows the general MPS3 pattern (a strongest line near 370 cm-1, a medium-strong line near 264 cm-1, a weak line near 241 cm-1, and a moderate line near 551 cm-1) plus a broad band at 123.5 cm-1, all in a 295 K spectrum. Compared with FePS3 at 290-300 K from two papers (Lee et al. arXiv:1608.04169 Fig. 1b and Fig. S7; Kim et al. arXiv:1906.05802 Fig. S3), the strongest sample lines are displaced from the FePS3 modes by more than the reading uncertainty and than the Si calibration allows: 263.5 cm-1 vs ~275-280 cm-1 (P5), 368.7 cm-1 vs ~372-383 cm-1 (P6). The broad band at 123.5 cm-1 has no FePS3 counterpart at 300 K (the FePS3 broad feature is near 100 cm-1), the 75 cm-1 line is unexplained, and the relative intensity of the 263.5 cm-1 line to the 368.7 cm-1 line is about twice the FePS3 ratio. The 240.7 cm-1 weak line and the 551 cm-1 moderate line are plausibly FePS3 P4 and P7 but P7 is weak in FePS3 at 300 K. Neither MnPS3 nor NiPS3 fits better. Conclusion: the spectrum is not consistent with bulk FePS3 at 295 K as read against these references. The mismatch is not explained by the Si calibration (+0.2 cm-1), the 532 nm laser, or the 295 K temperature, which is above TN of about 118-120 K, so the magnon near 122 cm-1 (McCreary et al. PRB 101, 064416) is not expected here.

Kim, K. et al., Antiferromagnetic ordering in van der Waals two-dimensional magnetic material MnPS3 probed by Raman spectroscopy, 2D Materials 6, 041001 (2019), arXiv:1906.05802, DOI 10.1088/2053-1583/ab27d5. Fig. S3 (FePS3, NiPS3 and MnPS3 Raman at 290 K and 10 K).

McCreary, A. et al., Quasi-Two-Dimensional Magnon Identification in Antiferromagnetic FePS3 via Magneto-Raman Spectroscopy, PRB 101, 064416 (2020), arXiv:1908.00608, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.101.064416. Abstract: TN about 120 K; magnon at about 122 cm-1 in the magnetically ordered state.
limits: Literature positions were read by eye from figures (about +/-2-3 cm-1). The two FePS3 papers disagree on the 300 K P6 position (about 372-378 vs about 383), so the P6 offset is only 3-14 cm-1, while the P5 offset of 12-17 cm-1 is more robust. Reference laser wavelengths and powers were not verified, and laser heating and power effects were not tested.

The reference spectra are bulk crystals. Thin flakes on SiO2/Si can shift modes by about 1-2 cm-1 and change relative intensities through interference, but I did not have a thin-flake FePS3 reference at 532 nm, so the sample's thickness and possible flake effects remain unknown.
The working folder holds only one 60-1100 cm-1 unpolarized spectrum. No angle series, so no polarization classes or irreps can be given, and mode labels rest on the literature pattern only.

Temperature is 295 K, above the Neel temperature of about 118-120 K. A magnon at about 122 cm-1 is therefore not expected, and the 123.5 cm-1 band should be phonon-like. The data cannot test magnetic ordering directly.

The skill's Computational Raman Database, reference notes and relation files sit outside this working folder, and I did not read them because of the folder restriction. The candidate ranking therefore uses only the two published FePS3/MnPS3/NiPS3 datasets above, not the full database.
I did not identify CdPS3 or ZnPS3 references. The working-folder name contains 'CdPS3'; I did not use that name as evidence and cannot test CdPS3 here.

Peak positions and widths come from local Voigt fits with a linear baseline. Standard errors are about 0.05-0.14 cm-1 for the strong lines and about 0.4-0.5 cm-1 for the weak ones. The point-to-point noise is about 400 counts against peak heights of 2-10 thousand counts, so weak bands (74.8, 240.7) and the broad 123.5 band are less certain.
Spike check: only the two adjacent high points at 520.4 and 521.3 cm-1 were flagged, and both belong to the Si line, so no cosmic-ray spikes were found and no artifacts are reported.
Layer number, strain, doping, defect density and phase could not be determined from this spectrum. No relation was applied, so properties are left empty.
